Episodes Discussion Thread: Season 6, Episodes 25 & 26, "To Where and Back Again" (Parts 1 & 2)

Some meandering musings:

Ever since Discord was reformed, I was wondering how they'd maintain dramatic tension and possibility of an antagonist victory with such a nigh omnipotent being. The solution presented here is kind of a cheat, but I'll accept it, as the reason for his loss of ability also serves as a plot device.

It also means that Starlight Glimmer can't use the magic she so often relies on to solve problems rather than friendship. This, for her, is the part in the hero's journey where her mentor is no longer available and they must put their teachings to use. Joseph Campbell would have been perplexed if she just magicked her way to the throne.

Speaking of which, I noticed one interesting theme in these episodes that may not have been intentional: Characters becoming overly reliant on their special abilities. We realize how out of his element Discord must feel when he's not able to use the powers that define him (he hadn't walked that far in millenia!), and how a skilled unicorn such as Starlight would feel the same way. (Shades of Twilight from Winter Wrap-Up day, I suppose.) In addition, we again see how changelings are so overconfident in their shapeshifting powers. Just as the Queen didn't put much effort into acting like Cadence when she was disguised as such, the Mane Six's impostors didn't even try to act nice and friendly to Starlight. In both cases, it contributed to be their defeat.

Another thing. The changelings' redemption may seem a bit overdone, but it was perhaps necessary. Changelings aren't necessarily evil, gryphons aren't all greedy and materialistic — such lessons might be necessary in order to avoid unfortunate implications, something about which I'd mentioned previously. I suppose we all need to accept that in the MLP:FiM universe, there exists no race of beings that are inherently and irreversibly different from others in terms of their morals and personality.
